comments.body:
STACK IS PHYSICALLY INVALID MID-CHAIN — needs a landing-strategy decision, not another rebase.

MEASURED runner.py at each stack position after rebasing onto current main (which is now 798 LOC in runner.py, up ~100 since this epic began):
  7468=795   f184=802 (OVER the 800 hard cap)   dc0d=815 (OVER)   2682=670
  2932=713   9249=713   281f=713 (all OVER 2682's attested <700 headroom test)   3a98=680
This matches the vote board exactly: 1012/1032/1081 green, 1014/1023/1043/1048/1067 Verified -1.

The chain grows runner.py BEFORE it splits it. Against the OLD main (~698) that was fine; against 798 the early changes breach immediately. Two distinct gates fire: the 800-LOC CI hard cap on f184/dc0d, and 2682's own <700 test on everything between 2932 and 3a98.

REORDERING DOES NOT WORK — attempted and aborted cleanly (backup ref kept, nothing lost). Two hard dependencies block it:
  (a) 2682 cannot precede dc0d: its split captured the POST-dc0d  signature (), so applying it earlier puts a caps-signature function in structured_run.py while runner.py still calls it with .
  (b) 3a98 cannot precede 2682: it moves code INTO structured_run.py, which 2682 creates.
So both shrinking changes are pinned AFTER the growing ones. The projected clean ordering (795/650/617/624/637/680/680/680) is unreachable without re-authoring closed stories' commits.

OPTIONS, none of which should be taken silently:
1. FEATURE BRANCH — the project's own documented answer for multi-story work (CONTRIBUTING.md S4: 'not one giant change or a fragile chain'). Review each story into refs/heads/feature/<name>, then ONE --no-ff merge change into main. CI gates the MERGE, so intermediate LOC states never gate. Requires feature-branch-driver rights, which RebarBotNava may not hold.
2. RE-AUTHOR 2682 to split against the pre-dc0d runner.py, then reorder. Substantial surgery on a CLOSED story's commit, and it would invalidate that story's attestation.
3. SHRINK runner.py inside 7468 by ~20 lines so f184 (802) and dc0d (815) fit under 800. Needs another movable seam in the FIRST change; providers.py (which 7468 creates) is at 299/300 so it cannot absorb it.

RECOMMENDATION: option 1. It is the documented mechanism for exactly this situation, it is the only one that does not re-author closed stories, and the chain is 8 deep — the fragility this epic hit is precisely what the feature-branch flow exists to avoid.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
OPERATOR DECISION: the per-FUNCTION length ratchet is REJECTED FOR NOW — blast radius too high.

This supersedes ADR 0056's standing recommendation, so record it here rather than let the next
session re-derive it. ADR 0056 §Decision 1 deferred a per-function gate and wrote: "If the pattern
recurs a fourth time, the per-function gate is the answer and should be raised as project-wide
work." I raised it, because the pattern HAS recurred — laterally, across six sibling files now
within 7 lines of the 800 cap rather than a fourth regrowth of runner.py. The operator has
considered and declined it.

THE REASON IS SOUND AND IS ALREADY IN THE ADR'S OWN NUMBERS: a per-function gate is not a change to
any one module. MEASURED across 3,292 functions under src/rebar — 21 over 200 lines, 38 over 150,
62 over 120, 101 over 100 — with the ten worst spanning six subsystems
(_mcp_writes.register_write_tools 352, plan_review.resign_plan_review 303,
_mcp_reads.register_read_tools 298, _run_plan_review 294, import_ndjson.import_tickets 273,
review_bot.review_and_vote 270). Adopting it would either break the build in six subsystems at once
or require an allowlist — and epic 716f deliberately DRAINED AND REMOVED the module-size
allowlist, so reintroducing that escape hatch would undo shipped work.

WHAT THIS CHANGES, stated plainly so the consequence is not lost: ADR 0056 named the residual risk
as "nothing structurally prevents the decomposed run() from regrowing", and the per-function gate
was the named remedy. With it declined, the module-level reworks are no longer a belt-and-braces
mitigation — THEY ARE THE ONLY DEFENCE, and they are a mitigation rather than a guarantee. Two
things follow:

 1. The SEAM TEST becomes the substitute ratchet, and is now load-bearing rather than nice-to-have.
    Change 1484 added `< 700` headroom assertions for gate_dispatch.py and orchestrator.py, and
    those two files are the comfortable ones today precisely because of it. The files that hurt now
    (config.py 793, passes.py 800, signing.py 798, workflow_ops.py 794, transition_close.py 793)
    have NO such guard, so nothing warns before a breach blocks a ticket mid-flight. Every
    hardening change should ship its own headroom assertion for the file it relieves.
 2. One existing guard is STALE and should be corrected while we are here:
    test_gate_dispatch_seam.py's gate_dispatch headroom test justifies itself with "adding an
    argument at its three finalize_verdict call sites is not a build break", but change 1484 moved
    those three call sites to workflow/plan_review_recovery.py. It guards a premise that no longer
    holds, and its prose at :4 plus plan_review_recovery.py:8 are stale the same way.

REOPENING TRIGGER, recorded so this is a deferral and not amnesia: if a hardening rework is itself
blocked by a single oversized FUNCTION that no file-level split can relieve — i.e. the mass is one
indivisible method rather than separable concerns — the per-function gate returns to the table as
scoped work on that subsystem, not as a project-wide ratchet.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
S6 (0d76-ebbf-ee3a-48ac) PARITY VERDICT, carried to this epic as a COMMENT rather than a
description edit — a description edit would be material and would invalidate this epic's
plan-review attestation at the worst point in the sequence (the epic closes last).

BEDROCK DID NOT CLEAR THE PARITY BAR. Both class slots were measured live in
896586841071/us-east-1 (30-item pooled gold corpus, 28 scored, N=3 epochs, 360 case-runs,
~15.4M input tokens):

  standard  bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6  FAILED — 1 decision-level flip (bar: 0)
  frontier  bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8    FAILED — 2 flips, agreement 0.929 < 0.95,
                                                     and the false-accept criterion

So the epic's "first-class provider" tier label for Bedrock is NOT earned by measurement today,
and S8 (eb6e) must not cut the production review bot over citing a cleared bar.

THE NUANCE MATTERS AND SHOULD NOT BE LOST: all three flips run in Bedrock's FAVOUR against the
gold labels — on standard it caught a gold-BLOCK case direct Anthropic missed (recall 0.857 ->
0.929), and on frontier it correctly declined to fire on two gold-ADVISORY cases direct
Anthropic false-fired on. Validity was 1.000 on both arms of both slots over 360 case-runs,
runtime error rate 0.000, latency at or better than direct Anthropic, and the v2 arms were
provably provider-clean (zero non-Bedrock calls). The failure is specifically the
"zero decision-level flips" criterion, not a quality regression.

Before Bedrock's first-class claim is re-litigated, the S6 comment thread recommends three
things in order: land 635f (the missing `errored` guard, which did not affect this run but would
fabricate flips on a flakier one); settle whether `parity._recall_false_accept` is inverted (it
computes specificity and the gate fails when it RISES, which is what failed the frontier slot);
and run the SAME harness Anthropic-vs-Anthropic to establish the bar's own noise floor at N=3 on
a 28-item gold set — the control this run lacks. If a same-provider run also flips, the problem
is the bar, and changing it is a deliberate decision for this epic, not something S6 may assume.

Full numbers, per-criterion breakdown, run provenance and the committed artifact
(`src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/provider_parity_results.json`, re-scored offline by
`tests/unit/test_provider_parity.py`) are on 0d76.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
S6 (0d76-ebbf-ee3a-48ac) — CORRECTED VERDICT under the rescoped criteria. This SUPERSEDES my
earlier comment on this epic, which said Bedrock did not clear the bar and that S8 must not cut
over. Recorded as a COMMENT, not a description edit, for the sequencing reason the AC states.

THE RESCOPE. The operator ruled that LLM non-determinism is expected and that comparing two
MODELS' judgements is OUT OF SCOPE for this epic. The epic's scope is that the same PAYLOADS
reach the LLM and the same TOOLS are available, regardless of model and provider. Under that
scope S6 PASSES.

WHAT IS PROVEN, from captured outbound requests rather than from reading code (both class slots,
zero network calls, zero tokens — the production path is aborted at the provider boundary):
  * PAYLOAD PARITY — system prompt, messages, max_tokens and temperature are equivalent across
    providers; the model id is the only differing field. The 8 provider-required envelope
    differences are enumerated.
  * TOOL PARITY — 6 tools, identical names, descriptions and input schemas.
  * CAPABILITY DIFFERENCES — one, explicit and symmetric: `temperature` is withdrawn from opus
    on BOTH providers and sent to sonnet on BOTH, driven by the model's capability record, not
    by the provider.
  * PROVIDER-CLEAN ROUTING — zero non-Bedrock calls across 84/84 v2 case-runs per slot.
  * INVOKABILITY — both Bedrock inference-profile ids invoke in 896586841071/us-east-1.

All four are regression-gated by offline tests in `tests/unit/test_provider_parity.py`, not just
observed once.

NOW INFORMATIONAL, NOT GATING: the paired-run ParityReport's decision flips (1 standard, 2
frontier) and the 0.929 frontier verdict agreement. They compare two different models'
judgements. Worth keeping for S8's benefit: all three flips ran in BEDROCK's favour against the
gold labels, validity was 1.000 on 360 case-runs, and the runtime error rate was 0.000.

CONSEQUENCE FOR S8 (eb6e): the cutover is NOT blocked by S6. Two measured facts should travel
with it — Bedrock's `cachePoint` cache marker carries no TTL where Anthropic's `cache_control`
carries one (latent today, rebar sets no non-default TTL), and per-case-run cost is far above
what the S6 plan assumed because the code-review arm is agentic (~100k input tokens, ~8.6
provider requests per case-run). Latency is at or better than direct Anthropic.

comments.body:
EPIC AC EVIDENCE SWEEP — each of the seven unticked criteria located or newly produced. No AC
checkbox is ticked by this comment; ticking is a MATERIAL edit and is being batched into ONE
edit followed by ONE plan review, so the attestation is paid for once.

--- AC1 "every child story is closed and its change is Verified +1" ---
18 children (16 stories + 2 tasks). Landed-commit census by `rebar-ticket:` trailer against
origin/main:
  4 commits: 0d76, f124 · 2 commits: 343b, c403, eb6e · 1 commit: 1aa2, 2932, 3768, 7468,
  8415, 9249, b690, dc0d, f184, 12e4, 5e75, 8625 · 0 commits: eb58
Every one of those commits reached main THROUGH Gerrit, which is only submittable at
`Verified +1`, so "its change is Verified +1" is established by the merge itself.
THE ONE EXCEPTION, recorded rather than ticked silently: eb58 ("Model classes:
trivial/standard/frontier as the universal LLM interface") has NO commit anywhere —
`git log --all --grep=eb58-e71d-ec90-4b00` returns only ticket-event commits. It is a
DECISION story: its deliverable was the class-system design (its own comments record a
keystone claim it got wrong and corrected under review) plus an operator-attested
two-provider gate run; the code implementing those decisions landed under 3768 and b690.
So AC1 reads as satisfied with eb58 vacuously rather than deficiently satisfied — there is no
change to be `Verified +1`, not a change that failed to be.

--- AC2 "review-plan AND verify-completion both green against Bedrock, evidenced on 2932" ---
HALF-MISFILED, now located. `review-plan` on Bedrock is recorded on 2932. `verify-completion`
on Bedrock is recorded — but on 1aa2 (S7b), not 2932, which is why 2932 has ZERO
verify-completion mentions. The 1aa2 record is first-hand and complete:
    Command: rebar verify-completion 1aa2-37cf-5cdf-48b7 --ref HEAD -o json
    provider=bedrock model=bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6 tier=first_class
    per-call tally: 1 call, 1/1 Bedrock, ZERO direct-Anthropic; cache_read NONZERO
    "GATE 3/3 verify-completion ON BEDROCK — EXERCISED, outcome recorded"
So the substance of AC2 exists; only its filing location differs from the AC's wording. Being
completed by attaching a consolidated record to 2932 (see the follow-up comment there).

--- AC4 "REBAR_LLM_BASE_URL composes with REBAR_LLM_API_KEY + REBAR_LLM_MODEL_PROVIDER" ---
NEWLY PRODUCED THIS SESSION, by execution against a live OpenAI-compatible endpoint. All four
clauses asserted in one probe:
 1. composition through LLMConfig.from_env():
      model=local-model  base_url=http://localhost:1235/v1  model_provider=openai
      api_key present=True
 2. ProviderSession.provider_factory("openai") returns
      rebar.llm.providers._RebarOpenAICompatibleProvider
      MRO: _RebarOpenAICompatibleProvider <- OpenAIProvider <- Provider <- ABC
      isinstance(provider, pydantic_ai.providers.openai.OpenAIProvider) is True
      provider.base_url == http://localhost:1235/v1/   (the local endpoint, as the AC requires)

      STUB_RECEIVED path=/v1/chat/completions model=local-model auth=True
    and the runner returned a completion whose own provider_provenance reads
      provider=openai model=openai:local-model endpoint_host=localhost
    No LLMConfigError was raised for base_url/api_key — the AC's `_pai_check_config` clause.
ALSO exercised against a genuine third-party server: this host runs LMStudio on :1234, and the
same composition reached it — a real OpenAI-shaped HTTP response came back (a 400 refusing to
load its own model), which proves the routing independently of my endpoint. The successful
completion above is cited from the deterministic endpoint on :1235.

--- AC5 "non-zero cache_read_tokens on the second of two identical calls" ---
ALREADY RECORDED on 2932, not re-run (the measurement is the pass condition):
    us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6: attempt 1 cache_write=4017 cache_read=0;

                             "model": "bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6",

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
CLOSING THE EPIC. All 8 acceptance criteria ticked, each against evidence recorded on this ticket
or a named child. Plan review PASS and SIGNED.

--- THE BLOCKER IS GONE ---
`129e-2d88-cce2-492c` (which `blocks` this epic — it is NOT a child; `parent_id` is null) is CLOSED
as `--class regression`, its change 1344 MERGED as 929ba5d669 with LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1.
Closing it emitted `UNBLOCKED: 061c-ecd1-8967-4a76`.
Story `8625-7bea-67db-4cdc` also closed, 4/4 ACs, with its doc correction merged as 996a3b107f.
All 18 children are closed.

--- THE PLAN REVIEW EARNED ITS COST: IT CAUGHT A FALSE CLAIM IN THIS EPIC'S OWN PLAN ---
First run: BLOCK, 1 blocking finding, criterion G6, severity critical. The plan's "Retry and
timeout on Bedrock" section presented a botocore mechanism as ACHIEVED —
`botocore.config.Config(retries={"max_attempts": …, "mode": "adaptive"})` threaded via
`BedrockProvider(bedrock_client=…)`, plus `aws_read_timeout`/`aws_connect_timeout` — and concluded
"the retry-attempt count and the read timeout are thus driven by the SAME LLMConfig fields on both
first-class providers, which is the parity S6 measures".
NONE OF THAT SHIPS. `bedrock_model.py:101` is a bare `BedrockProvider(region_name=region)`: no
botocore Config, no adaptive mode, no timeout kwargs. So `llm_retry_max_attempts`,
`llm_retry_max_wait_s` and `timeout_s` do not reach Bedrock at all; the tenacity envelope and
`httpx.Timeout(read=cfg.timeout_s)` exist only on the direct-Anthropic path
(`anthropic_model.py:113-125`, `providers.py:219`). Production runs on Bedrock, so the UNCONFIGURED
path is the live one.
The finding was correct and I accepted it rather than arguing: the already-merged ADR 0059 records
the same limitation under "Negative, and deliberately accepted", `docs/llm-framework.md` states it
as one of three limits an attestation consumer must know, and bug [rebar:61d8-ff23-8ee0-4289]
tracks it. The reviewer also corrected the MECHANISM: the right shape is
`BedrockProvider(bedrock_client=…)`, not the `aws_read_timeout` kwarg this plan proposed.
FIX APPLIED to this description: the paragraph is now marked corrected, states what actually ships,
says plainly that `first_class` does NOT currently mean retry/timeout parity and that S6 does not

Second run: PASS, 0 blocking, 6 advisory, SIGNED at head_sha 929ba5d669.
Two paid reviews, not one, and the first paid for itself.

--- THE SIGNED VERDICT'S OWN PROVENANCE, which is AC6 demonstrated on this epic ---
    {"provider": "bedrock", "model": "bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6",

# LLM provider seam — first-class Bedrock + best-effort OpenAI-compatible, with tiered verdict provenance

## Context / Problem

rebar's LLM runtime is provider-agnostic in principle but Anthropic-shaped in practice. `runner.py:268`
branches on `resolved.startswith("anthropic")` to build the retrying transport; `runner.py:316` gates prompt
caching on the same string; `structured.py:46` picks the output mode from a hardcoded
`_NATIVE_OUTPUT_PROVIDERS` name set; and `runner.py:653` (`_pai_check_config`) REFUSES `base_url`/`api_key`
outright. That refusal was deliberate — commit `75e598a41` records it as "a loud guard that REFUSES
base_url/api_key rather than silently dropping them (a capability gap vs langgraph, surfaced not hidden)" —
but `docs/llm-framework.md:126-133,226` already documents `REBAR_LLM_BASE_URL`/`REBAR_LLM_API_KEY` as working,
and `config.py:502-503,611-612` already parses them. The documentation is currently false.

Meanwhile our clients will reach Claude through **AWS Bedrock more often than through the direct Anthropic
API**, and rebar has no Bedrock path at all. GitHub PR #120/#121 surfaced this: #121 proposed fronting Bedrock
with an OpenAI-compatible gateway, which works but silently gives up prompt caching, the retrying tenacity
transport, the per-request read timeout, and native structured output — and records a `model` string in the
SIGNED verdict sidecar (`plan_review/sidecar.py:601`, `completion_sidecar.py:206`) that no longer names what
actually answered.

## Approach

Adopt pydantic-ai's own extension points instead of inventing rebar-specific ones.

1. **Seam = `provider_factory`.** pydantic-ai's `infer_model()` accepts a `provider_factory` hook; upstream
   issue pydantic-ai#1343 explicitly directs user-configurable-provider apps to it rather than patching
   `infer_provider`. rebar keeps `provider:model` strings as the single selector (already the design in
   `anthropic_model.py:159` `_pai_model`) and supplies ONE factory that returns configured `Provider` objects.
   The inline anthropic branch at `runner.py:268` becomes a factory entry, not a special case.
2. **Capabilities = `ModelProfile`.** pydantic-ai exposes a per-vendor capability profile at `model.profile`.
   Output-mode selection and cache settings read the profile instead of matching provider name strings.
   Bedrock-hosted Anthropic gets a rebar `ModelProfile` override, which is the documented upstream guidance
   precisely because Bedrock's capability flags differ from the direct Anthropic API.
3. **Two support tiers.** First-class = Anthropic + Bedrock: native builders, full fidelity, covered by tests
   and the parity bar. Best-effort = everything else through one OpenAI-compatible builder.
4. **Provenance carries the tier.** The signed sidecar's `model` field widens to structured provenance
   (provider, model, endpoint host, tier, effective capabilities) so a consumer can tell a first-class verdict
   from a best-effort one.
5. **Dogfood on the review bot.** The AWS-hosted code-review bot cuts over to Claude via Bedrock.

**Retry and timeout on Bedrock are botocore's, not httpx's.** `BedrockConverseModel` reaches AWS through a
boto3/botocore client, **not** an `httpx.AsyncClient`, so the `AsyncTenacityTransport` built by
`anthropic_model._build_retrying_anthropic_model` does not and cannot wrap it. "Full fidelity" for the
first-class tier was therefore INTENDED to mean **equivalent retry and timeout guarantees achieved per
transport**, not the same transport object on both providers — an intention that, as recorded below, was
not delivered. **CORRECTED AFTER EXECUTION — this paragraph originally described the botocore mechanism below as
ACHIEVED, and it is NOT.** What actually ships is a bare `BedrockProvider(region_name=region)`
(`bedrock_model.py:101`): no `botocore.config.Config`, no `adaptive` mode, and no
`aws_read_timeout`/`aws_connect_timeout`. So `llm_retry_max_attempts`, `llm_retry_max_wait_s` and
`timeout_s` **do not reach Bedrock at all**, and the tenacity retry envelope plus
`httpx.Timeout(read=cfg.timeout_s)` exist ONLY on the direct-Anthropic path
(`anthropic_model.py:113-125`, `providers.py:219`). Since production runs on Bedrock, the
UNCONFIGURED path is the live one.

**So `first_class` does NOT currently mean retry/timeout parity, and S6 does not measure it.** The
intended mechanism — a `botocore.config.Config(retries=...)` threaded via
`BedrockProvider(bedrock_client=...)`, which is the correct shape rather than the
`aws_read_timeout` kwarg this plan first proposed — is DEFERRED to bug
[rebar:61d8-ff23-8ee0-4289] and was undesigned when that bug was filed. The already-merged
ADR 0059 records the same limitation under "Negative, and deliberately accepted", and
`docs/llm-framework.md` states it as one of the three limits an attestation consumer must know.
Everything else the `first_class` tier claims — a native rebar builder, capabilities derived from
the real `ModelProfile`, unit-suite and provider-parity coverage — is delivered; retry/timeout is
the one named exception.

**Capability assertions verified against the pinned pydantic-ai (1.107.1, `pydantic-ai-slim>=1,<2`).** Each
mechanism this epic depends on was resolved in the worktree venv before the plan was accepted, so none of the
following is an unverified assumption:

- `pydantic_ai.models.infer_model(model, provider_factory: Callable[[str], Provider[Any]] = infer_provider)`
  — the hook exists with exactly the single-positional-`str` signature S1's factory must match.
- `BedrockConverseModel.__init__(model_name, *, provider, profile: ModelProfileSpec | None = None, settings)`
  — the `profile` parameter **is** the caller-supplied `ModelProfile` override injection path S2 needs; no
  monkeypatching of `infer_provider` is required.
- `BedrockModelSettings` carries `bedrock_cache_instructions`, `bedrock_cache_tool_definitions` **and**
  `bedrock_cache_messages`; the direct-Anthropic `AnthropicModelSettings` carries the first two only. So the
  Bedrock cache surface is a superset, and S3's caching claim is implementable as described.
- `BedrockModelProfile` already declares the capability flags that differ from direct Anthropic —
  `bedrock_supports_prompt_caching` and `bedrock_supports_tool_caching` (plus
  `bedrock_supports_tool_choice`, `bedrock_supports_strict_tool_definition`, `bedrock_thinking_variant`).
  These are the flags the rebar override table records.
- The flags S2 reads to replace the hardcoded `_NATIVE_OUTPUT_PROVIDERS` name set are
  `ModelProfile.supports_json_schema_output`, `ModelProfile.supports_json_object_output` and
  `ModelProfile.default_structured_output_mode`.

**Alternative rejected: LiteLLM as an in-process SDK** (the aider / OpenHands pattern). It buys 100+ providers
for one dependency, but its normalization layer is documented to drift on exactly what rebar depends on —
prompt-cache semantics, tool-call shapes, and cost accounting — and neither aider nor OpenHands escapes
per-provider code anyway (OpenHands still carries a `model_features.py` registry and two auto-detected
completion modes). rebar chose pydantic-ai for weight and structured-output reliability; adding LiteLLM
in-process would duplicate its model layer. A LiteLLM *proxy* remains reachable through the best-effort
OpenAI-compatible builder, so breadth is preserved without the dependency.

**Alternative rejected: gateway-only Bedrock** (PR #121's approach). It requires every operator to stand up and
accredit a proxy, and gives up caching, thinking, native structured output, and the retrying transport. The
native `BedrockConverseModel` path needs no proxy and supports prompt caching via `BedrockModelSettings`.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/runner.py` — replace the inline anthropic branch (`:268`) and the cache gate (`:316`) with
  factory + profile lookups; retire the `_pai_check_config` refusal (`:653`).
- `src/rebar/llm/anthropic_model.py` — the anthropic builder moves behind the factory; `_pai_model` (`:159`)
  stays the string resolver.
- `src/rebar/llm/structured.py` — `output_mode` (`:51`) reads the profile instead of `_NATIVE_OUTPUT_PROVIDERS`
  (`:46`).
- `src/rebar/llm/config.py` — `base_url`/`api_key`/`model_provider` (`:501-503`) composition semantics.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sidecar.py`, `src/rebar/llm/completion_sidecar.py` — provenance payload.
- `src/rebar/llm/parity.py` — the Bedrock-vs-Anthropic parity run.
- `pyproject.toml` — a `[bedrock]` optional extra.
- `infra/terraform/main.tf` (`:50-54` `metadata_options`), `infra/terraform/iam.tf`, `infra/scripts/fetch-secrets.sh`.
- `docs/llm-framework.md`, `docs/env-vars.md`, a new ADR.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] every child story is closed and its change is `Verified +1` on Gerrit. All 18 children (16 stories + 2 tasks) are closed. Every landed commit reached `main` THROUGH Gerrit, which is submittable only at `Verified +1`, so the merge itself establishes the vote. ONE EXCEPTION, recorded rather than ticked silently: `eb58-e71d-ec90-4b00` has NO commit anywhere (`git log --all --grep=eb58-e71d-ec90-4b00` returns only ticket-event commits). It is a DECISION story — its deliverable was the model-class design plus an operator-attested two-provider gate run, and the code implementing those decisions landed under `3768-789c-11ed-48be` and `b690-f232-5bae-4b8b`. So for eb58 this criterion is VACUOUSLY satisfied (there is no change to be `Verified +1`), not deficiently satisfied.
- [x] [operator-attested] `rebar review-plan` **and** `rebar verify-completion` both run green against Bedrock
      in a live env-gated check, evidenced by the run output attached as a comment on the Bedrock story
      (S3, `2932-8a98-6d70-4550`)
- [x] No module selects provider behavior by matching a provider-name string, and every pydantic-ai
      `Provider` object is constructed WITHIN THE PROVIDER-MODULE COLLECTION — `src/rebar/llm/providers.py`
      together with the leaf builders it delegates to (`bedrock_model.py`, `anthropic_model.py`). AMENDED
      (operator-authorised) from the original wording, which required construction inside `providers.py`
      ITSELF: the architecture deliberately moved construction OUT to leaf builders, recorded at
      `providers.py` `_build_bedrock` — "the construction logic lives THERE, not here ... only the registry
      entry — never a provider's construction body — belongs in `ProviderSession`" — so that the file stays
      well under the module-size cap. The invariant that actually matters is UNCHANGED and still holds: the
      provider-name -> builder MAPPING happens only in `providers.py`'s registry, and a leaf module owns
      construction only, never selection. Verified: the only `Provider` constructions are
      `bedrock_model.py` `return BedrockProvider(region_name=region)` and `anthropic_model.py`'s
      `AnthropicProvider(anthropic_client=...)`, both reached solely through the registry's builder slots.
      One residual prefix match exists and is NOT provider selection — `anthropic_model.py`'s
      `_anthropic_web_search_capabilities` gates a per-model CAPABILITY on `resolved.startswith("anthropic")`.
      It is a real defect against the zero-exceptions rule, is tracked as [rebar:129e-2d88-cce2-492c], and is
      being removed there in favour of a profile-derived decision; the attested guard
      `test_capabilities_module_still_has_no_provider_name_prefix_matching` is not weakened by either change.
- [x] `REBAR_LLM_BASE_URL` works as `docs/llm-framework.md:126-133,226` already claims, **composing with
      `REBAR_LLM_API_KEY` and `REBAR_LLM_MODEL_PROVIDER`**: with all three set, a gate call is routed through
      the best-effort OpenAI-compatible builder to that endpoint with that key, and `_pai_check_config` no
      longer raises `LLMConfigError` for `base_url`/`api_key`. Worked example — `REBAR_LLM_MODEL_PROVIDER=openai`,
      `REBAR_LLM_BASE_URL=http://localhost:11434/v1`, `REBAR_LLM_API_KEY=sk-local` builds an `OpenAIProvider`
      whose `base_url` is `http://localhost:11434/v1`, and the run's provenance records tier `best-effort`.
- [x] [operator-attested] A gate run against AWS Bedrock Claude reports a **non-zero `cache_read_tokens` on the
      second of two identical calls** (read back via `_extract_usage`). **The measurement is the pass condition,
      not the outcome**: if caching measures ineffective, S3 records the two observed usage dicts and the
      diagnosed reason as a comment on its ticket and the epic still passes. An *unattempted* or *unrecorded*
      measurement does not pass.
- [x] A signed verdict states which provider, endpoint host, and support tier produced it
- [x] the review bot's most recent `LLM-Review` vote on a real change carries Bedrock provenance in its sidecar
- [x] [operator-attested] The production review bot votes `LLM-Review` using Bedrock with **no direct-Anthropic
      fallback**, and a CloudWatch alarm on the review bot's Bedrock `InvokeModel` client-error rate — threshold
      >25% of invocations over a 15-minute window, 2 consecutive periods — publishes to the review bot's
      existing SNS notification topic. Evidence: the alarm ARN and one forced test notification recorded on
      S8 (`eb6e-f43a-e86b-443a`).
